prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a member in hospital during a claim. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member is in hospital, I should slow the claim down at the start and confirm the best contact is a relative, carer or solicitor before I chase for details, because the member may not be able to respond reliably."},{"type":"fact","content":"When hospitalisation affects their ability to manage the claim, I should note any power of attorney, deputyship or documented representative authority early, so I only speak to the right person within delegated authority."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member is admitted for several days, I should prioritise urgent mitigation and safety checks first, then come back for non-critical documentation once the immediate risk is contained."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member is in hospital, I should keep updates short, plain and reassuring, because long or technical explanations are harder for families to relay accurately."},{"type":"observation","content":"When I cannot reach the member directly, I should ask whether another household adult can confirm the loss details, but I should still verify ownership, occupancy and incident timing carefully."},{"type":"fact","content":"When treatment or recovery means the member may not remember dates clearly, I should cross-check the timeline against repair reports, call notes and any emergency service records before I set reserves or liability decisions."},{"type":"observation","content":"When hospitalisation is linked to the insured event, I should avoid assumptions about causation and separate the medical issue from the home or motor loss unless there is clear evidence they are connected."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member is worried about missing deadlines from hospital, I should proactively extend reasonable response times and tell them what I need next, so the claim keeps moving without pressure."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is not fit to discuss loss details, I should still arrange inspections, temporary repairs and hire support where appropriate, because those steps do not always need the member present."},{"type":"observation","content":"When family members are involved, I should be careful to record who said what and whether they are relaying the member's view or their own, because mixed information can easily distort the claim file."}]}
